skill.name: attribution-reconciler
skill.description: Reconcile paid-platform conversions against GA4 or ecommerce order exports, remove duplicate credit, normalize windows and currencies, compare models, and assess holdout incrementality.
skill.summary: Build recurring attribution workbooks from order-level truth sets and paid-platform exports.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

content.value_statement: Advertising platforms often claim the same sale or use incompatible windows and currencies. This skill reconciles claims against real orders and reports normalized, de-duplicated attribution.
actual_capabilities: Matches platform-reported conversions to a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID truth set.
Labels conversions as matched, double-counted, or unmatched.
Normalizes attribution windows and currencies before comparing platform claims.
Compares credit allocation across at least two attribution models.
Calculates holdout lift when test and control exports are available.
Creates a recurring reconciliation workbook and saves it only after user approval.
limitations: Requires an order-ID export and cannot reconcile from platform totals alone.
Timestamp and value matching is less reliable when order IDs are unavailable.
Cannot estimate incrementality without a valid geo or holdout test.
Does not calculate ROAS, CPA, ROI, or organic dark-social attribution.

use_cases.title: Audit Monthly Paid Conversions
use_cases.description: Reconcile Meta and Google claims against ecommerce orders before monthly reporting.

use_cases.title: Standardize Cross-Platform Reporting
use_cases.description: Normalize windows and currencies for comparable channel reporting.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Campaign Incrementality
use_cases.description: Compare holdout lift with last-click attribution for budget decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicate Conversion Claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile these Meta and Google exports against my GA4 order export. Label every claim as matched, double-counted, or unmatched.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with order IDs and two platform exports.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Monthly Attribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize these platform exports to [window] and [currency]. Then show de-duplicated conversions by platform against the attached ecommerce orders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Monthly reporting across different windows and currencies.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Attribution Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile the attached orders and platform claims. Compare last-click with [linear or position-based] allocation using only de-duplicated real orders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced credit-allocation analysis for the same order set.

prompt_templates.title: Read Holdout Incrementality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these test and control exports to calculate lift. Compare incremental orders with last-click claims and explain any attribution gap.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incrementality assessment with a valid holdout.

output_examples.input: GA4 orders plus Meta and Google conversion exports for May.
output: 1,240 platform claims mapped to 1,010 verified orders.
145 orders were claimed by both platforms.
85 claims had no matching order and require review.

output_examples.input: Meta seven-day data and Google thirty-day data in different currencies.
output_examples.output: Both exports were normalized to a seven-day window and USD. The comparison shows de-duplicated verified orders by platform.

output_examples.input: Test-region and control-region orders from a two-week geo holdout.
output_examples.output: The holdout indicates 8.4 percent lift, while last-click claimed 13.1 percent. The 4.7-point gap suggests over-attribution.

best_practices: Provide stable order IDs, timestamps, values, currencies, and platform attribution windows.
Choose the common window and conversion currency before matching records.
Review unmatched claims and approve any persistent workbook storage.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a platform conversion total as the order truth set.
Do not compare exports before normalizing attribution windows and currencies.
Do not infer incrementality from attribution data without a control group.

faq.question: Which export is required?
faq.answer: A GA4 or ecommerce order export with order IDs is required. Platform conversion exports are also needed for reconciliation.

faq.question: Can it reconcile Meta and Google together?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies orders claimed by multiple platforms and counts each verified order once.

faq.question: What happens when order IDs are missing?
faq.answer: It can match timestamps and values as a fallback, but the result is less reliable.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROAS or CPA?
faq.answer: No. It prepares clean conversion counts for a separate ratio or ROI calculation workflow.

faq.question: Can it measure incrementality?
faq.answer: Yes, when valid test and control exports exist. Otherwise, it marks incrementality as unavailable.

faq.question: Does it save customer order data?
faq.answer: It asks before saving a reconciliation workbook. Users should review storage policies before approving persistent files.
